question:
Read the below statements marked as Assertion (A) and Reason (R). Mark the correct option:

Assertion (A): India is working on constructing a Third Launch Pad at SDSC-SHAR.

Reason (R): The proposed pad aims to support frequent launches and accommodate heavier future rockets like NGLV.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R explains A
Both A and R are true, but R does not explain A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true

solution:
The correct answer is __**Both A and R are true, and R explains A.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Assertion (A): India is working on constructing a Third Launch Pad at SDSC-SHAR.**

 
 
• The **Satish Dhawan Space Centre (SDSC-SHAR)**, located in Sriharikota, Andhra Pradesh, serves as the primary launch site for the **Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO)**.
 
• The construction of the **Third Launch Pad** is a part of ISRO’s long-term vision to enhance its space exploration capabilities.
 
• This new launch pad aims to accommodate the increasing number of launches planned by ISRO, especially with the growing demand for satellite deployment. *Hence, statement A is correct.*
 
 
 
• **Reason (R): The proposed pad aims to support frequent launches and accommodate heavier future rockets like NGLV.**
 
 
• The Third Launch Pad is designed to facilitate **frequent launches**, addressing the growing demand for commercial satellite launches and advanced space missions.
 
• It will also support the launch of **heavier rockets**, such as the **Next Generation Launch Vehicle (NGLV)**, which is in development to meet future space exploration needs.
 
• The NGLV, as planned by ISRO, will be capable of carrying heavier payloads and will be more cost-effective for various missions, including those for national security and interplanetary exploration. *Hence, statement R is correct.*
 
 
 
• Since the Reason (R) directly explains the Assertion (A), it establishes a cause-and-effect relationship. ISRO’s decision to build a Third Launch Pad aligns with the objective of addressing the increasing demand for launches and the development of advanced launch vehicles. *Thus, the correct option is: Both A and R are true, and R explains A.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Satish Dhawan Space Centre (SDSC-SHAR):**

 
 
• **Location:** Sriharikota, Andhra Pradesh.
 
• It is India’s primary spaceport, used for launching satellites into orbit.
 
• It currently has two operational launch pads: the **First Launch Pad (FLP)** and the **Second Launch Pad (SLP)**.
 
• Both these pads are used to launch Polar Satellite Launch Vehicles (PSLVs), Geosynchronous Satellite Launch Vehicles (GSLVs), and other rockets.
 
 
 
• **Third Launch Pad:**
 
 
• **Purpose:** To support increased launch frequency, accommodate heavier rockets, and reduce dependence on the existing two launch pads.
 
• The additional pad will be critical for launching new-generation rockets like the **NGLV** and **manned space missions** under the Gaganyaan program.
 
• It will also help India cater to the growing global demand for satellite launches.
 
 
 
• **Next Generation Launch Vehicle (NGLV):**
 
 
• **Purpose:** To replace PSLV and GSLV with a more advanced, cost-effective launch vehicle.
 
• **Payload Capacity:** The NGLV is expected to carry payloads of up to **10 tons** to Geostationary Transfer Orbit (GTO) and **20 tons** to Low Earth Orbit (LEO).
 
• **Design:** A three-stage vehicle with options for solid, liquid, and semi-cryogenic propulsion.
 
• **Applications:** Launch of satellites, interplanetary exploration missions, and manned spaceflights.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **ISRO’s Space Programs:**

 
 
• **Gaganyaan Mission:** India’s first human spaceflight program, scheduled for launch in the near future.
 
• **Chandrayaan Missions:** Lunar exploration missions, including the successful Chandrayaan-3 landing on the Moon’s South Pole in **2023**.
 
• **Mangalyaan:** India’s first interplanetary mission to Mars, launched in **2013**.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Launch Pads:**
 
 
• Launch pads are essential for assembling, testing, and launching rockets into space.
 
• They provide critical infrastructure, including fueling systems, launch control centers, and ground support systems.
 
• Having multiple launch pads ensures operational flexibility and increases the capacity for conducting frequent launches.
